title: The Slash Subject Line Kit: [Your Company] / [Their Company]
description: The slash subject line a famous founder swears by, why it works, and 4 steps to write the email that goes with it.
lead: This is the Slash Subject Line Kit from the reel. One punctuation mark makes your cold email look like a shared project instead of an ad.
insider: We test subject lines on every campaign before we scale. In one small pilot, that testing helped get a **4% reply rate and 103 sales opportunities from 10,284 people**. A good subject line gets the open. A good list and offer get the reply, and that's the system we build for clients.

blocks.label: Subject line formula
blocks.text:
[Your company] / [Their company]

Examples:
WayneFlow / Acme
BrightPath / Summit Dental

Jesse Itzler shared this on X and says it works a lot. David Ogilvy said five times as many people read the headline as the body, and your subject line is the headline. A slash looks like an internal project between two companies, not a sales email.

items: No emojis, no "free", no capital letters shouting.
Line one is about them: their new office, their new hire, their new product.
End with one small ask: "Worth a look?"

blocks.label: Prompt
blocks.text:
My company: [name], what we do: [one sentence].
Prospect company: [name], website: [link].

Write a cold email with the subject "[my company] / [their company]". First line: something specific and recent about them. Then one sentence on the result we could get them. End with "Worth a look?". Under 70 words, plain text, no emojis.

faq.q: Does this work for every industry?
faq.a: It works best in B2B, where a partnership between two companies makes sense. Test it against your current subject line on two small lists.
Write company names the normal way. Just avoid ALL CAPS and spammy words.
